script.base: Market prices a close CIN road win in a moderate 46.5 game, not a shootout and not a slog. BAL still feeds Derrick Henry (65 carries, 233 yards over weeks 4-6) because CIN allows 5.30 YPC, but that run volume has already coexisted with Zay Flowers at 10 targets a game, so Flowers stays the intermediate option in a one-score script. CIN, facing BAL's 31% blitz and a Burrow EPA drop to -0.11 when blitzed, leans quick and short, which is Chase Brown's receiving role (17 targets, 3 air yards over weeks 3-5), rather than a pure Higgins vertical script.
script.flip1: CIN leads by 14 early and clocks it with Brown and Perine. BAL abandons the run, Flowers' targets spike as BAL throws to catch up, and Brown's receiving volume dies because CIN stops dropping back. Flowers over survives; Brown rec over does not.
script.flip2: BAL jumps ahead and closes with Henry (CIN's 5.30 YPC run defense invites it). Pass attempts fall, Flowers stalls under 64.5, and CIN throws to catch up so Brown's checkdowns stay live. Brown rec over survives; Flowers over does not.

Brown is the CIN checkdown (17 targets, 100 rec yards, 3 air yards) into the 31% blitz that already makes Burrow less efficient. Higgins (363 air yards, 13.4 aDOT) attacks the vertical/perimeter, which is not where BAL bleeds, so he is not the overlap.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Baltimore saw 5.30 YPC and gave Henry a 25-plus carry grind in a 20-17 game, cutting Flowers to 5 targets and about 48 yards, under 64.5. Brown's receiving over lost because the 31% blitz turned into sacks and throwaways instead of checkdowns, and the short targets that did come out went to Gesicki and Perine, leaving Brown at 3 catches for 14 yards. The one-score, both-offenses-functional script never held, and a missing wind or inactive note that was not in the pack would have been the step that caught it.
slip_story: One competitive-game story at CIN -3 and 46.5: both passing games stay on schedule, not a Henry clock-kill stack and not a shootout overs stack. Flowers over is the BAL intermediate attack into CIN's middle; Brown rec over is CIN's answer to BAL's blitz. They share the base script and each survives a different flip, so a blowout either way breaks one leg. Keep it to these two, no TDs, no receptions, no passing yards.
